fixes.explanation: Yes, friend. Verse 50 says the sword cut off the servant's right ear. The text is exact about which side. That's the ear Jesus touches in verse 51.
That's the one, baker. Jesus tells them, “Pray that you will not enter into temptation.” No long speech and no fine print, just one clear thing to pray. He says it again in verse 46.

Nothing about the city or a message comes up here, baker. Jesus keeps it close to home and tells them, “Pray that you will not enter into temptation.” It's short and simple. That's what He asks them to pray, and He repeats it in verse 46.

Elijah does appear and speak with Jesus in another scene (Luke 9:30-31). But he's not in this one. Here the text says an angel from heaven appeared to Him and strengthened Him. Different scene, friend.
Moses does appear and speak with Jesus in a different moment (Luke 9:30-31). Not here, though, baker. In this passage, “…an angel from heaven appeared to Him and strengthened Him.” That's the one.
That's right, baker. Verse 45 says Jesus found them asleep, exhausted from sorrow. Then He asks, “Why are you sleeping?” That question comes in verse 46.
Praying is a fair guess, friend. But when Jesus returned, He found them asleep. Then He asks, “Why are you sleeping?” They weren't praying.
Feet come to mind, since Jesus washes His disciples' feet in John 13:5. But that isn't what Judas approaches Him to do here, baker. Verse 47 says he approached Jesus to kiss Him.
That's him, baker. Verse 50 says one of them struck the servant of the high priest. The high priest was the top priest. The text doesn't name the swordsman or the servant here.
Judas is the one who walked up to Jesus, so he'd be the natural guess. But verse 50 says the man struck the servant of the high priest, friend. That's who took the hit.
Not the left one, friend. Verse 50 says it was his right ear. This is a heavy moment, so it's worth reading slowly.
Not an arm, friend. Verse 50 says the sword cut off his right ear. And in verse 51, Jesus touches the man's ear and heals him.

Swords can make you think soldier, friend, and I get it. But Jesus is speaking to the chief priests, temple officers, and elders, and His question is, “Have you come out with swords and clubs as you would against an outlaw?” Outlaw is the word He picks.
It's the reverse, baker. Jesus says, “Every day I was with you in the temple courts, and you did not lay a hand on Me.” Every day, and no hand laid on Him. That's what He tells them.

Right, friend. Jesus says, “Every day I was with you in the temple courts, and you did not lay a hand on Me.” So all those days in the temple, no hands laid on Him. He says it to the chief priests, temple officers, and elders who had come for Him.
Rome is a fair guess, baker, but Jesus doesn't name it in what He says. He says, “But this hour belongs to you and to the power of darkness.” That last part is what He names.

I can see why that one tempts you, friend, but Jesus doesn't say it. He says it to the chief priests, temple officers, and elders who had come for Him: “But this hour belongs to you and to the power of darkness.” It's a heavy line, so I'd read it slowly.
